text.title: Kestrel
text.menu_sub: Soar over the forest, catch beetles, roost in the trees.
text.menu_wild: Foxes catch you on the ground.
text.intro: Hold Fly to climb, Dive to drop. Roost in tree leaves at night.
text.hungry: You're hungry. Look for beetles on the ground.
text.no_food: Nothing to eat here. Look for beetles on the ground.
text.chased: A fox is after you! Take to the air!
text.about_looks: A small falcon with a long tail. The male has a grey head; the female is brown all over.
text.about_food: Mostly voles. Also big insects and small lizards.
text.about_home: It doesn't build a nest. It lays its eggs in an old crow's nest, a hole in a tree or a nest box.
text.about_winter: Flies south in autumn, to southern Europe or Africa, and comes back in April.
text.about_young: Eggs are laid in May. The chicks leave the nest in early summer.
text.about_fact: A kestrel can hang still in the air, facing into the wind, while it looks for voles below.

year.shelter: Doesn't build: nests in an old crow's nest, a tree hole or a nest box, and roosts in trees.
year.young: Eggs in May, chicks fledge in late June–July.

food.autumn: Voles and insects before flying south.
food.winter: Away: winters in southern Europe and Africa.

year.notes: Vole years decide how many chicks it raises. In winter it should be away from Nuuksio.
